test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 03
subject: general
question: A wall 18 m long, 10 m high and 40 cm wide is to be constructed using bricks of dimensions 30 cm, 15 cm and 10 cm. How many bricks (in thousands) will be required?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all dimensions to **cm**: **Wall** = 1800 × 1000 × 40 | **Brick** = 30 × 15 × 10

Number of bricks = (1800 × 1000 × 40) ÷ (30 × 15 × 10)

Number of bricks = 60 × 66.67 × 4 = 16000 bricks

Required answer in **thousands** = 16000 ÷ 1000 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of wall (L) = 18 m = 1800 cm

Height of wall (H) = 10 m = 1000 cm

Width of wall (W) = 40 cm

Brick dimensions = 30 cm × 15 cm × 10 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/295d0c7a454ad4876a8d5017990a6e5894ae0d8222825640bce4ef5b3ef7a427.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cuboid = Length × Width × Height

Number of Bricks = Volume of Wall ÷ Volume of 1 Brick

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of Wall = 1800 × 1000 × 40 = 72,000,000 cm³

⇒ Volume of 1 Brick = 30 × 15 × 10 = 4,500 cm³

⇒ Total Bricks = 72,000,000 ÷ 4,500

⇒ Total Bricks = 16,000

⇒ Bricks in thousands = 16,000 ÷ 1000 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Consistency

Always ensure all dimensions (Length, Width, Height) are in the same unit (cm or m) before calculating volume. 1 m = 100 cm.

Volume of a Cuboid

The amount of space occupied by a 3D rectangular object is given by V = l × b × h.

Number of Items

When a larger object is formed by smaller identical objects, the total number = (Total Volume) ÷ (Volume of one small item).</p
